entities.name: One Thousand and One Nights
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Collection of Middle Eastern folk stories created by an unknown author in the 8th century CE, spanning over 1,000 nights and influencing Arabic literature and Islamic culture.

This body of work is considered one of the greatest literary achievements in human history, with translations into many languages and adaptations across various cultures.

The One Thousand and One Nights has had a profound impact on Western literature, inspiring works such as Voltaire's 'Zadig' and influencing authors like Goethe and Scott.

Its themes of love, betrayal, and redemption continue to captivate audiences worldwide, with its stories often featuring strong female characters and complex moral dilemmas.
